evaluation.summary: A deliberate, well-communicating AI-driven worker: strong prompt craft (no brief-pasting, real iteration, verification asks), clarifying questions before building, a maintained decision log, and clean adaptation to the mid-flight requirement change, with work that clearly diverges from the unattended baseline. questions.decision: Flagged the divergent threshold constant in devcase-run.ts in the decision log but shipped with the flaw left in place rather than unifying the two sites
questions.question: In your decision log you called out the threshold inconsistency in devcase-run.ts but chose not to fix it. Walk me through that call: what were the two sites involved, why did you leave the divergence in, and what would have had to be true for you to unify them instead?
questions.listenFor: Names both concrete locations and the actual values, articulates a real risk that made fixing it out-of-scope (blast radius, unknown downstream consumers, no test coverage to protect the change), and can say precisely what evidence would have flipped the decision.
questions.redFlag: Remembers that something was flagged but not what or where; explains the flag as 'the tool mentioned it'; treats fixing vs. flagging as equally fine with no criterion for choosing between them.

questions.decision: The confidence-vs-score conflation in devcase-run.ts propagated into the submission untouched
questions.question: Let's open devcase-run.ts together at the spot where confidence and score interact â€” take a minute and tell me what you see there and whether you'd ship it as-is today. If something bothers you, when in your process would you normally have caught it, and why didn't that happen this time?
questions.listenFor: Spots the conflation live or reasons toward it from the semantics ('confidence measures how sure the extractor is, not how good the candidate is'); honestly reconstructs why their review pass missed it â€” e.g. they diffed their own edits but never audited pre-existing lines their change depended on.
questions.redFlag: Cannot engage with the code they nominally submitted; reads the line aloud without noticing the semantic mismatch; or claims they reviewed every line but can't say what a correct version would look like.
